test.name: Escalate to search-external-sites after FamilySearch census exhaustion
test.description: When a FamilySearch census search returns nil across 3+ name variants for an important plan item and the question remains open, the skill must invoke Skill('search-external-sites') to generate Ancestry/MyHeritage search URLs. FamilySearch's index has no phonetic fallback — a transcription error (e.g. 'Flynn' → 'Flinn') means no variant will ever surface that record on FamilySearch. Other sites fuzzy-match and can recover it, which is exactly why the escalation is triggered by the nil signal here, not planned upfront. search-external-sites is stubbed with a canned response rather than executed: compute_allowed_tools unions the tools of plugin agents referenced via @plugin:<name> but NOT of sub-skills invoked via Skill(...), so the callee runs with neither place_search nor external_links_search and improvises a URL from prose. Measured in v1_2026-07-30_19-24-10, where it said so itself — 'The place_search and external_links_search tools aren't available in this environment' — and produced a URL with no name_x=ps_ps, the phonetic flag this escalation exists to obtain. Stubbing is therefore closer to the real behaviour than running it here, not further from it, until the union gap is fixed in the harness.

input.user_message: Execute pli_001 — search FamilySearch for Patrick Flynn in the 1850 US census.

stub_skills.response:
Ancestry — 1850 US Federal Census, Patrick Flynn (phonetic/partial name matching enabled, which is the point of leaving FamilySearch):
https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/8054/?name=Patrick_Flynn&name_x=ps_ps&birth=1845_Ireland&residence=1850_Schuylkill-County-Pennsylvania

Ancestry — site-wide fallback across all collections, same phonetic flag:
https://www.ancestry.com/search/?name=Patrick_Flynn&name_x=ps_ps&birth=1845_Ireland

No MyHeritage or FindMyPast links: researcher_profile lists no subscription to either. Logged as an external_site entry with outcome 'partial' (URL generated, capture not yet received). Next step is for the researcher to open these in their own authenticated browser and upload the PDF capture.

judge_context: This is a POSITIVE test for the FamilySearch-exhaustion → external-sites escalation. After trying 3+ FamilySearch name variants for Patrick Flynn (all returning zero results), the skill MUST call Skill('search-external-sites').

DO NOT grade whether Skill('search-external-sites') was invoked — a deterministic validator (test_escalates_to_external_sites_after_fs_exhaustion) owns that assertion and reads the harness's own record of the call. Judging it from the transcript has produced false failures. Grade only the quality of the surrounding work: the variants tried, the triage, and the log entries.

The plan item pli_001 must NOT be marked 'completed' as if the search succeeded — it should remain in_progress or be logged as a nil result awaiting external follow-up, because the external search has not yet been run.
The nil log entry must be written (research_log_append called) with outcome 'negative', results_examined 0, and notes that FamilySearch variants were exhausted and external sites should be checked.
Acceptable: the skill may also mention research-plan as an alternative path. But it must escalate — suggestion alone without the Skill call is a Correctness=1 failure.

Tool Arguments: score 3 if primary searches include givenName on every call. Score 2 if a primary search drops givenName without having first tried givenName variants. Score 1 if multiple primary calls systematically omit givenName.

DO NOT grade the Ancestry URLs in any way — not their composition (collection id, parameter names, which sites, whether MyHeritage/FindMyPast appear) and NOT their provenance. They came back from the search-external-sites hand-off; building them is that skill's job, covered by its own suite (eval/tests/unit/search-external-sites/). They are genuine by construction, so 'are these real or placeholders?' is not a question this test asks and you have no way to answer it — a judge scored Correctness=1 on 2026-07-31 by guessing 'placeholder URLs' about links that were in fact relayed verbatim. Grade only the escalation decision and the FamilySearch work around it.
